title: Unit 2: Characteristics and Classification of Organisms
description: Comprehensive questions covering Grade 9 Biology Unit 2

questions.question: What is the fundamental difference between unicellular and multicellular organisms?
options: Unicellular organisms lack a nucleus; multicellular organisms have a nucleus
Unicellular organisms are made of one cell; multicellular organisms are made of many cells
Unicellular organisms cannot reproduce; multicellular organisms can reproduce
Unicellular organisms are only prokaryotes; multicellular organisms are only eukaryotes
questions.correctAnswer: Unicellular organisms are made of one cell; multicellular organisms are made of many cells
questions.explanation: Unicellular organisms like bacteria consist of a single cell, while multicellular organisms like plants and animals are composed of many cells.

questions.question: Which characteristic of living things explains why a plant bends toward sunlight?
questions.explanation: Sensitivity is the ability to detect and respond to stimuli in the internal or external environment. A plant bending toward sunlight is responding to the stimulus of light.

questions.question: The permanent increase in size and mass due to an increase in cell number or cell size is known as:
questions.explanation: Growth is defined as a permanent increase in size and mass resulting from an increase in cell number, cell size, or both.

questions.question: Which process involves the removal of metabolic wastes produced in cells as a result of chemical reactions?
questions.explanation: Excretion is the removal of metabolic waste products produced in cells from chemical reactions such as respiration.

questions.question: Organisms that use energy from sunlight to make their own food through photosynthesis are called:
questions.explanation: Autotrophs (producers) make their own food using sunlight through photosynthesis. Heterotrophs cannot make their own food and consume others.

questions.question: Homeostasis refers to:
options: The ability to move from place to place
The regulation of an organism's internal conditions to maintain stability
The increase in size and mass of an organism
questions.correctAnswer: The regulation of an organism's internal conditions to maintain stability
questions.explanation: Homeostasis is the regulation of internal conditions to maintain stability, such as keeping body temperature constant despite external changes.

questions.question: What is the science of naming, identifying, and classifying organisms called?
questions.explanation: Taxonomy is the branch of biology concerned with naming, identifying, and classifying organisms.

questions.question: Who is known as the father of taxonomy?
questions.explanation: Carolus Linnaeus (1707–1778) was a Swedish botanist who introduced the taxonomic hierarchy and binomial nomenclature, earning him the title 'father of taxonomy'.

questions.question: The Greek philosopher who developed the first widely accepted biological classification system was:
questions.explanation: Aristotle (384-322 BC) developed the first widely accepted biological classification system, using simple morphological characters to classify plants into trees, shrubs, and herbs.

questions.question: Which of the following lists the taxonomic hierarchy from the broadest to the most specific rank?
options: Species, genus, family, order, class, phylum, kingdom, domain
Domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species
Kingdom, domain, phylum, class, order, family, species, genus
Domain, kingdom, class, phylum, order, family, genus, species
questions.correctAnswer: Domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species
questions.explanation: The taxonomic hierarchy from broadest to most specific is: domain, kingdom, phylum (or division for plants), class, order, family, genus, species.

questions.question: In plant taxonomy, the term used instead of 'phylum' is:
questions.explanation: Plant taxonomists use the term 'division' instead of 'phylum' as a rank in the taxonomic hierarchy.

questions.question: What is a taxon (plural: taxa)?
options: A type of microscope used to identify organisms
A rank in a taxonomic hierarchy
A laboratory technique for classifying organisms
A type of cell found only in plants
questions.correctAnswer: A rank in a taxonomic hierarchy
questions.explanation: Each rank in a taxonomic hierarchy is termed a taxon. For example, kingdom, phylum, and class are all taxa.

questions.question: Which two kingdoms did Linnaeus include in his original classification system?
questions.explanation: Linnaeus developed a two-kingdom system classifying all organisms into Plantae and Animalia. This system did not distinguish between prokaryotes and eukaryotes.

questions.question: Which domain do protists, fungi, plants, and animals belong to?
questions.explanation: Domain Eukarya includes all eukaryotic organisms with a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles, including protists, fungi, plants, and animals.

questions.question: Archaea are prokaryotic organisms that:
options: Often inhabit extreme environments such as swamps and deep-ocean hot vents
Have a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles
questions.correctAnswer: Often inhabit extreme environments such as swamps and deep-ocean hot vents
questions.explanation: Archaea are prokaryotes that often live in extreme environments like swamps, deep-ocean hot-water vents, and seawater evaporating ponds. Unlike bacteria, their cell walls do not contain peptidoglycans.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes a species?
options: The broadest category in biological classification
A group of organisms that can reproduce to produce fertile offspring
Organisms that share the same habitat
questions.correctAnswer: A group of organisms that can reproduce to produce fertile offspring
questions.explanation: A species is the smallest natural group of organisms, defined as a group that can reproduce to produce fertile offspring and closely resemble each other.

questions.question: What is the correct way to write the scientific name for humans?
questions.explanation: In binomial nomenclature, the genus name starts with a capital letter, the specific epithet with a small letter. Scientific names are italicized when printed or underlined when handwritten.

questions.question: The binomial system of naming organisms was introduced by:
questions.explanation: Linnaeus refined and popularized the binomial system in which the first name represents the genus and the second name the specific epithet.

questions.question: In the scientific name Zea mays, what does 'Zea' represent?
questions.explanation: In binomial nomenclature, the first name represents the genus. Zea is the genus, and mays is the specific epithet (species).

questions.question: Why are scientific names preferred over common names?
options: Scientific names are shorter and easier to remember
Scientific names are universally recognized and avoid confusion across languages
Scientific names change frequently to match new discoveries
Scientific names describe the habitat of the organism
questions.correctAnswer: Scientific names are universally recognized and avoid confusion across languages
questions.explanation: Common names vary by language and region (e.g., maize, corn, Bekolo). Scientific names in Latin form are recognized worldwide regardless of language barriers.

questions.question: Ethiopia is considered a primary centre of diversity for which of the following crops?
options: Noug (Guizotia abyssinica), tef (Eragrostis tef), and Ethiopian mustard (Brassica carinata)
questions.correctAnswer: Noug (Guizotia abyssinica), tef (Eragrostis tef), and Ethiopian mustard (Brassica carinata)
questions.explanation: Ethiopia is a primary centre of diversity for noug, tef, and Ethiopian mustard, as well as having wide diversity in barley, sorghum, durum wheat, and other crops.

questions.question: The Ethiopian wolf is scientifically known as:
questions.explanation: Canis simensis is the scientific name for the Ethiopian wolf, which belongs to the family Canidae and order Carnivora.

questions.question: To which genus does the gelada monkey belong?
questions.explanation: The gelada monkey's scientific name is Theropithecus gelada. It belongs to the family Cercopithecidae and order Primate.

questions.question: The Walia ibex (Capra walie) belongs to which family?
questions.explanation: Capra walie (Walia ibex) belongs to the family Bovidae and order Artiodactyla. It is endemic to Ethiopia.

questions.question: What is the scientific name of the African elephant found in Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: Loxodonta africana is the African bush elephant, belonging to the family Elephantidae and order Proboscidea.

questions.question: Enset (false banana) belongs to which family?
questions.explanation: Enset (Ensete ventricosum) and banana (Musa acuminata) both belong to the family Musaceae.

questions.question: What is a dichotomous key used for?
options: Identifying unfamiliar organisms through paired contrasting features
questions.correctAnswer: Identifying unfamiliar organisms through paired contrasting features
questions.explanation: Dichotomous keys consist of pairs of contrasting features (dichotomous means two branches). By following the key and making choices, an unknown organism can be correctly identified.

questions.question: Who proposed the five-kingdom system of classification?
questions.explanation: Robert Whittaker (1969) proposed the five-kingdom classification system consisting of Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia.

questions.question: Which kingdom includes organisms with prokaryotic cells and no membrane-bound organelles?
questions.explanation: Kingdom Monera includes simple prokaryotic unicellular organisms that lack a well-defined nucleus and membrane-bound organelles. It includes eubacteria and archaebacteria.

questions.question: Bacteria that can make their own food using chemical reactions rather than sunlight are called:
questions.explanation: Some autotrophic bacteria make energy by chemical reactions rather than photosynthesis. These are called chemosynthetic bacteria.

questions.question: Eubacteria differ from archaebacteria in that eubacteria:
questions.explanation: Eubacteria (true bacteria) have cell walls containing peptidoglycans, while archaebacteria have very different cell walls that do not contain peptidoglycans.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of kingdom Monera?
options: Presence of rigid cell walls in most members
questions.explanation: All members of Monera are unicellular prokaryotes. They lack a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles, and most have rigid cell walls.

questions.question: What is the single common feature shared by all protists?
questions.explanation: Protists are extremely diverse, but they all share one feature: they are eukaryotes, meaning their metabolic processes take place inside membrane-bound organelles.

questions.question: Protozoans are protists that resemble which kingdom?
questions.explanation: Protozoans are animal-like protists. They are single-celled but share characteristics with animals, such as being heterotrophic and mobile.

questions.question: Which group of protists is photosynthetic and forms the basis of aquatic food chains?
questions.explanation: Algae are plant-like protists that are photosynthetic and autotrophic. Unicellular algae are the basis of aquatic food chains and produce much of Earth's oxygen.

questions.question: Fungi differ from plants mainly because fungi:
options: Are heterotrophic and cannot make their own food
questions.correctAnswer: Are heterotrophic and cannot make their own food
questions.explanation: Unlike plants which are autotrophic, fungi are heterotrophic. They cannot make their own food; instead, they absorb nutrients from their environment.

questions.question: The thread-like structures that make up the body of multicellular fungi are called:
questions.explanation: Fungal bodies consist of long, slender thread-like structures called hyphae. Hyphae play an important role in how fungi obtain food by secreting enzymes and absorbing nutrients.

questions.question: Fungal cell walls are made of:
questions.explanation: Fungi possess cell walls made of chitin and polysaccharides, which is different from plant cell walls made of cellulose.

questions.question: Fungi that absorb soluble organic matter from dead substrates are called:
questions.explanation: Saprophytes (decomposers) are fungi that absorb nutrients from non-living organic material such as fallen logs, animal corpses, and wastes.

questions.question: Yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) is economically important because it is used for:
options: Making bread rise and producing alcoholic beverages
questions.correctAnswer: Making bread rise and producing alcoholic beverages
questions.explanation: Yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) is used to make injera rise (bread-making) and to produce alcoholic beverages such as Tej, Tella, and Beer.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of kingdom Plantae?
options: Cells with a cell wall made of cellulose
questions.correctAnswer: Cells with a cell wall made of cellulose
questions.explanation: Plants are multicellular, eukaryotic autotrophs. Their cells contain a rigid cell wall made of cellulose, and they have chloroplasts with chlorophyll for photosynthesis.

questions.question: Plants that lack vascular tissues and are seedless are called:
questions.explanation: Bryophytes (mosses, liverworts, hornworts) lack vascular tissues (xylem and phloem) and do not produce seeds.

questions.question: Seed plants that produce 'naked' seeds (not enclosed in an ovary) are classified as:
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms are seed plants that do not make flowers or fruits. Their seeds are 'naked', not enclosed in a floral ovary (e.g., conifers).

questions.question: Angiosperms are distinguished from gymnosperms because angiosperms:
questions.explanation: Angiosperms are flowering plants that produce seeds enclosed within a fruit (a mature ovary). Gymnosperms do not produce flowers or fruits.

questions.question: Monocots are a group of angiosperms characterized by:
options: Two seed leaves and branching leaf veins
One seed leaf and parallel leaf veins
questions.correctAnswer: One seed leaf and parallel leaf veins
questions.explanation: Monocots have one seed leaf (cotyledon) and parallel leaf veins. Examples include grasses, maize, and tef.

questions.question: All animals are characterized by being:
options: Able to make their own food through chemosynthesis
questions.explanation: Kingdom Animalia includes all multicellular, heterotrophic, eukaryotic organisms. Animals consume food obtained from other organisms.

questions.question: Unlike plants and fungi, animal cells lack:
questions.explanation: Animals lack the structural support of cell walls. Instead, animal cells are held together by structural proteins, primarily collagen.

questions.question: Which two types of specialized cells are found in most animals but not in other multicellular organisms?
options: Guard cells and root hair cells
questions.explanation: Many animals have muscle cells for movement and nerve cells for conducting impulses. These are organized into muscle tissue and nervous tissue.

questions.question: Animals are broadly divided into two groups based on:
options: The presence or absence of a backbone
questions.correctAnswer: The presence or absence of a backbone
questions.explanation: Animals are classified into invertebrates (no backbone) and vertebrates (with a backbone).

questions.question: Which of the following is a correct list of vertebrate groups?
options: Fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals
Sponges, flatworms, roundworms, annelids, and arthropods
questions.correctAnswer: Fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals
questions.explanation: Vertebrates include fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals. The other options list invertebrate groups or plant groups.

questions.question: According to the textbook, which of the following is an example of an Ethiopian plant that contains chemicals used as a disinfectant?
questions.explanation: Moringa stenopetala (Shiferaw) is mentioned as a tree containing chemicals that make good disinfectants. Closely related species could have the same useful substances.

questions.question: Viruses are not classified into any kingdom because they:
options: Are too small to be studied
Lack key characteristics of living things such as growth and respiration
Can only be found in extreme environments
questions.correctAnswer: Lack key characteristics of living things such as growth and respiration
questions.explanation: Viruses are not considered living organisms because they don't grow, develop, or carry out respiration. They need a host cell to replicate.

questions.question: Which Ethiopian taxonomist contributed to the Flora of Ethiopia and served as Chair of the Biological Society of Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: Professor Sebsebe Demissew published books on Ethiopian vegetation and plants, served as Chair of the Biological Society of Ethiopia, and as Secretary-General of AETFAT.

questions.question: Which Ethiopian taxonomist is a zoologist who contributed to the field of animal taxonomy?
questions.explanation: Professor Abebe Getahun is mentioned as one of the few zoologists who contributed to the field of animal taxonomy in Ethiopia.

questions.question: What method do fungi use to obtain nutrients?
options: Ingesting food and digesting it internally
Secreting enzymes to digest food externally and then absorbing the nutrients
Absorbing nutrients directly from the soil through roots
questions.correctAnswer: Secreting enzymes to digest food externally and then absorbing the nutrients
questions.explanation: Fungi use extracellular digestion: they secrete powerful enzymes into their surroundings, break down complex molecules, and then absorb the smaller organic compounds.

questions.question: Tef (Eragrostis tef) belongs to which family?
questions.explanation: Tef (Eragrostis tef) belongs to the family Poaceae (grass family), along with maize and wheat. It is in the class Lilospida and order Cyperales.

questions.question: Which taxonomic rank includes similar families?
questions.explanation: An order is a taxon of similar families. Multiple families with shared characteristics are grouped into an order.

questions.question: A genus consists of a group of:
questions.explanation: A genus (plural: genera) consists of a group of similar species. For example, the genus Panthera includes lions, tigers, and leopards.

questions.question: One reason classification is relevant to agriculture and medicine is that:
options: It determines the color of an organism
It helps discover new sources of lumber, foods, medicines, and energy
It allows farmers to grow any crop anywhere
It prevents all diseases in plants and animals
questions.correctAnswer: It helps discover new sources of lumber, foods, medicines, and energy
questions.explanation: Taxonomy can help the economy by discovering new sources of lumber, foods, medicines, and energy. If one species has useful chemicals, a closely related species might as well.

questions.question: The lion (Panthera leo) and the Ethiopian wolf (Canis simensis) are placed in different families because:
options: They belong to different orders—Felidae and Canidae respectively
One is herbivorous and the other is carnivorous
They are found on different continents
questions.correctAnswer: They belong to different orders—Felidae and Canidae respectively
questions.explanation: Lions belong to the family Felidae (cat family), while Ethiopian wolves belong to Canidae (dog family). Both are in the order Carnivora but are different families.

questions.question: How did Aristotle classify animals in his early system?
options: Into those with red blood and those without red blood
questions.correctAnswer: Into those with red blood and those without red blood
questions.explanation: Aristotle divided animals into those that had red blood and those that did not. He also classified plants into trees, shrubs, and herbs based on simple morphology.

questions.question: The body of a multicellular fungus is composed of a network of hyphae collectively called:
questions.explanation: The network of hyphae that makes up the body of a multicellular fungus is called mycelium. Fruiting bodies are distinct structures where spores are produced.
